language.script_notes: Turkish signage; Kurdish is the mother tongue for most people east of the Euphrates and Arabic is spoken in border areas; Kurdish warnings have been added on some pedestrian-crossing signs in Diyarbakır and Mardin, and bilingual Syriac and Turkish signs appear at monasteries around Mardin.

road_furniture.curb_style: As national; wide highways across open plains.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: As national; large-holed metal utility poles and red-and-white corner arrows.

architecture.roof_style: Flat roofs are standard on traditional stone houses, often used as terraces in the hot summer nights.
architecture.roof_material: Flat stone and earth on old houses; concrete slab on modern ones.
architecture.wall_construction: Heavy, thick-walled stone construction built around a central courtyard with an iwan (open vaulted hall) — creamy white-yellow limestone in Mardin, cascading in terraces down a hillside above the Mesopotamian plain, and dark grey-black basalt in Diyarbakır, whose mighty basalt city walls loom over the Tigris; concrete apartment blocks in the modern cities.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Honey-yellow limestone in Mardin, dark basalt in Diyarbakır, and sun-bleached tan concrete elsewhere.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Terraced limestone towns above the plain (Mardin); Diyarbakır's black basalt walls and mosques with striped stonework; the Balıklıgöl sacred pools and mosques in Şanlıurfa; Roman mosaics and citadels in Gaziantep.

nature.vegetation: Open cotton, wheat and lentil fields and pistachio orchards on the plain; almost treeless rolling steppe outside irrigated valleys, turning brown and dusty by mid-summer.
nature.terrain: A broad, hot plain in the northern Mesopotamian basin drained by the Euphrates and Tigris, with rolling limestone hills, plateaus and dammed reservoirs.
nature.climate_signature: Hot, dry and dusty summers and mild winters; a sun-bleached tan-and-gold look far from the green Black Sea or snowy east.

vehicles.plate_color: As national — province codes such as 27 (Gaziantep), 21 (Diyarbakır), 47 (Mardin), 63 (Şanlıurfa).
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Tractors and pickup trucks; motorbikes, minibuses and heavy trucks on the highways to the border.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mostly Gen 3, with some older imagery.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Coverage follows main highways and city centres; border areas are thin or missing.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared northern Mesopotamian plain, similar stone architecture and dry landscapes across the border
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Latin-script signs with ı and ş, TR plates and orderly national road furniture; Syria and Iraq have essentially no official Street View coverage, so coverage here is almost certainly Turkish.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Similar dry steppe and stone settlements in border districts
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Persian script and plates differ from Latin-script signs and TR plates.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same national road furniture and plates
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The southeast is hot, flat and stone-built with limestone and basalt cities; the west is greener and denser, and the east is high and snowy.
